title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (February 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: the publisher's own standing rule, restated on conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 332,031 bytes after one 301) — "The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index (R) at 10 a.m. ET on the last Tuesday of every month." 2027-02-23 is the last Tuesday of February 2027. Verified for FEBRUARY specifically against four primary-sourced editions, each fetched direct 2026-09-06 at HTTP 200 and each checked against its own "Source: February <year> Consumer Confidence Survey" line and "Updated:" date rather than trusted by slug: CCI-Feb-2023 (Updated 2023-02-28), CCI-Feb-2024 (2024-02-27), CCI-Feb-2025 (2025-02-25), and the Board's PRNewswire distribution us-consumer-confidence-inched-up-in-february-302695754 (dateline "NEW YORK, Feb. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/", "Feb 24, 2026, 10:00 ET"). Every one is the last Tuesday of its February. Three of the four are DOUBLE-sourced by the preceding January edition's own next-release line -- CCI-Jan-2023 "next release is Tuesday, February 28", CCI-Jan-2024 "Tuesday, February 27th", CCI-Jan-2025 "Tuesday, February 25th". No February-2027 announcement exists yet, so this is the publisher's rule applied forward against a verified February record rather than a posted date. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: PROPOSED TWICE on 2026-09-06 -- by the consumer-confidence-2027-01-26 sweep (as its de-confounded CONTROL) and by the fhfa-hpi-2027-02-23 sweep (as the LAST CONFOUND standing on its own session) -- and researched the same day; both proposal files are now shadowed by this canonical one and were read before it was written. INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-06 (docs/research/events/consumer-confidence-2027-02-23.md) RAN THE CONTROL AND IT CAME BACK EMPTY, which answers both proposers at once. Of 68 rule-derived CB release days since 2021, 17 collide with an FOMC day and 51 are clean. The collision is a FOUR-MONTH property, not January's alone: January 6/6 and JULY 6/6, April 3/6, October 2/5, February 0/6 -- so a study controlling only for January still reads a confounded July. Clean CB days (n=51) differ from baseline on 0 of 9 instruments with NO near-miss (smallest p 0.26; SPY 0.910/0.982 p=0.4083); clean vs collision head to head is 0 of 9 (SPY 0.910/0.898, p=0.4529); D+1 after a clean print is 0 of 9; and dropping the five December dates the last-Tuesday rule is known to get wrong leaves 0 of 9 with every p >= 0.35. So the January lane's confound was never load-bearing, and the FHFA lane's "largest remaining confound" worry is measured at 0 of 9 at daily-bar resolution. A TRAP IS DOCUMENTED: February is a wide MONTH and the print is not why -- all 115 February sessions since 2021 clear p<0.05 on 4 of 9 vs the rest of the year (SPY 1.115/0.968 p=0.0426, VIX close 19.860/17.875 p=0.0208), but February CB days against OTHER February sessions are 0 of 9 (SPY 1.310/1.115, p=0.5172, n=6). That independently reproduces, on a different release series and instrument set, the same control failure the fhfa-hpi-2027-02-23 ledger documented. ALSO: the January sibling's "read the level, never the delta" aid is a MONTHLY property, not a January artifact -- February restates January 4 of 4 (107.1->106.0, 114.8->110.9, 104.1->105.3, 84.5->89.0) and March-2025 restates February by +1.8. IMPACT STAYS medium, matching the series. What this edition uniquely carries is informational rather than tradable: cut-off lags of 6/8/6/7 days put its panel at roughly 2027-02-01 -> 2027-02-16, closing 11 days BEFORE fomc-blackout-start-2027-03-06, so unlike the January edition (which prints inside the blackout) Fed officials can publicly react to it, and it is the ONLY CB edition between the Jan 26-27 and Mar 16-17 meetings. symbols: [] and 0 hits for any macro- or sentiment-keyed playbook in trade-playbooks.md or multi-symbol-sweep.md (re-grepped 2026-09-06); nothing here licenses an entry.
